henry.title: Explorers on the Moon and at Mercury
henry.mission: Put three real exploration events in order, then write a game log of what you see on Mercury today.
henry.done: The timeline is in order, both year problems are done, and your game log is written.
words: a machine sent to study space
a first-hand record of the date, the place, and what you saw

flow.title: Three dates, in order
flow.teach:
NASA Space Place: on July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin were the first people to set foot on the Moon. The Apollo 11 crew also included Michael Collins, who stayed in orbit.

NASA: Mariner 10 was the first spacecraft sent to Mercury. It flew past Mercury in 1974. MESSENGER orbited Mercury from 2011 to 2015.

People have walked on the Moon. People have not walked on Mercury. Spacecraft studied Mercury.

Example of years between, using different years: 2015 - 2011 = 4. That is the length of MESSENGER's orbit mission. Your problems use other years.
flow.sheet:
Put these in order, earliest first:
A. Mariner 10 flies past Mercury (1974)
B. MESSENGER begins orbiting Mercury (2011)
C. Apollo 11 lands on the Moon (1969)
1st ______ 2nd ______ 3rd ______
Years between, show the subtraction:
a) From Apollo 11 to Mariner 10: ______
b) From Apollo 11 to MESSENGER's orbit: ______
Have people walked on Mercury? ______ Name one spacecraft that studied it: ______

flow.title: A game log from today
flow.teach:
A log is a first-hand record: the date, the place, and what you saw. Armstrong's Moon landing is a record from 1969. Your log is a record of the game today. It is not a record of the real Mercury from the past.

Look for a crater (a round pit), a cliff (a long steep edge), or a plain (wide flat land). You might see something else. That is fine.
pics: Drive with W A S D. A grown-up reads the place name.
flow.sheet:
My game log for today
Date: __________
Place name from the screen: __________
I saw (circle any): crater / cliff / plain / other __________
One sentence about the most interesting thing I saw: ________________________________

henry.challenge: Optional. Space Place says the Moon has almost no atmosphere. On a windy day on Earth, what can the air do that the Moon's air cannot?
henry.adult:
Your setup time is not part of his 15 minutes. Open Regolith yourself. Press H and follow H if it disagrees. Do not overwrite a save. Land once on Mercury. He uses only W A S D. A readable name is enough. Discovery Rupes or Caloris Planitia are useful if you can read them. A cliff or bright rays may not show. Do not require them.

Sources checked on the NASA pages: Space Place Moon (July 20, 1969; Armstrong and Aldrin; almost no atmosphere). NASA Mariner 10 page: closest flyby March 29, 1974. The lesson says only that it flew past in 1974. NASA MESSENGER page: the story says orbit began at 00:45 UT on March 18, 2011, while a key-dates line on the same page says Mar. 11, 2011. The mission end on that page is April 30, 2015. The lesson uses only the years 2011 and 2015.

The bootprint photo is a real Apollo picture, not the game: NASA bootprint photo.

This build was not driven for these lessons. Skip Titan, Io, and Europa. Do not use jumps or speed as science.

parentKey.assess: Score the order, both subtractions, the spacecraft answer, and a complete game log. Do not grade which shapes he saw. The challenge is not scored.

items.a:
Order: C 1969, then A 1974, then B 2011.
a) 1974 - 1969 = 5.
b) 2011 - 1969 = 42.
People have not walked on Mercury. Spacecraft: Mariner 10 or MESSENGER.
Today's date, the place name you opened, at least one circle or the word other, and one complete sentence. It is a log of the game, not a historical record of Mercury.
Earth's air can blow things. The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so it does not have wind like Earth.

frankie.title: Bootprint and Round Pits
frankie.mission: Look at the real Moon bootprint photo, count round pits you see in the game, and write pit.
frankie.done: You circled the real photo, wrote a count for each stop, matched the words, and wrote pit.

flow.title: The real photo
flow.teach: Grown-up, open the photo and say: a real astronaut made this bootprint in 1969. It is not the game.
flow.sheet: Circle one: the real 1969 bootprint photo / the rover game today.

flow.title: Three short looks
flow.teach: Grown-up, you already landed on Mercury for Henry, or you land now. Frankie drives a little with W and stops three times. At each stop he counts round pits he can see. Zero is allowed.
pics: A crater is a round pit.
sheets: Round pits I see. Stop 1 ____   Stop 2 ____   Stop 3 ____
Stretch, only if you want it: add the three numbers. ____

flow.title: Read and write pit
flow.teach: Grown-up, name the pictures first: a hole for pit, a map, a cap.
sheets: Draw a line. Words: pit, map, cap. Pictures: cap 🧢   hole 🕳️   map 🗺️.

Circle every on: A pit is on the map. I am on it.
Trace: I see a pit.
Write pit: __________

frankie.adult: Use the same Mercury landing as Henry. He does not need a cliff. The photo link is the NASA bootprint, not the game.

parentKey.assess: Score the photo circle, the three counts, the word match, and writing pit. Adding the counts is optional.

items.a: He circles the real 1969 bootprint photo.
Three counts that match what he pointed at, including zero.
Optional. The sum of his three counts.
pit to the hole, map to the map, cap to the cap.
Both on words circled. He traces the sentence and writes pit.
